title: Clinical Outcomes Following Non‐Surgical Periodontal Therapy of Intrabony Defects With Narrow or Wide Radiographic Angle. A Short‐Term Retrospective Analysis
html:
ABSTRACT

Aim

To evaluate the clinical outcomes of non-surgical periodontal therapy (NSPT) in intrabony defects with narrow (< 37°) or wide (≥ 37°) radiographic defect angle (RDA).

Material and Methods

Forty-nine patients with 135 defects (61 with RDA < 37° and 74 with RDA ≥ 37°) were screened from the Biobank of King's College London. Probing depth (PD), clinical attachment level (CAL), gingival recession (GR) and bleeding on probing (BOP) were assessed at baseline and after 3 months. The percentage of pocket closure was also evaluated. Additional subgroup analysis between narrow and wide defects with shallow (≤ 4 mm) or deep (> 4 mm) intrabony component was performed. The primary outcome was PD change.

Results

Clinical parameters significantly improved after 3 months (p < 0.05); however, no statistically significant changes (p > 0.05) were found between narrow and wide defects. At 3 months, the mean change of PD was 1.7 ± 2.2 and 2.0 ± 2.2 mm for the narrow and wide defects, respectively. The proportion of pocket closure was 27% and 37.7% for narrow and wide defects, respectively. No statistically significant difference (p > 0.05) was noted. Multilevel regression analysis showed that PD was a negative predictor (OR = 0.675) of pocket closure.

Conclusions

Within the study limitations, these results indicate that NSPT improves clinical outcomes of narrow and wide defects. Baseline RDA did not affect the outcomes of NSPT. Short follow-up and the absence of wide/deep defects represent the major limitation, so the results cannot be generalised to all intrabony defects.
